title: Planning team config
description: Schema for a repository's docs/conventions/planning.yaml: the team layer of the planning plugin's settings. A value here overrides the same key in the plugin's userConfig. Contract: docs/adr/0064-home-plugin-customization-in-docs-conventions-yaml.md. question_pacing, answer_audit_rounds and wayfind_suggest_questions are read from <home>/planning.yaml in a bound convention home, and from <home>/planning.local.yaml above it (docs/adr/0075-resolve-plugin-settings-through-one-four-layer-cascade-and-a-bound-convention-home.md).

written_against.description: The plugin version the setup writer last wrote this file against, as <plugin>@<version>. The writer owns it; it is not a setting.

provenance.description: Per setting, whether the team chose the value or it was filled at the plugin default. The writer owns it; it is not a setting.

plan_store.description: Where /planning:plan keeps an approved plan. local: PLAN.md in the memory slice only. tracker: also posted as one marked comment on the claimed work item, updated in place on re-publish.

plan_reader.description: How much of an approved plan /planning:plan publishes to the work item or pastes into the pull request. step-by-step: the whole plan. standard: the Brief, the Design section and a phase outline. guardrails: the Brief and the Design section, with its conventions followed, net-new and challenged-pattern lines. A --reader argument overrides it for one run.

phase_order.description: How /planning:plan orders phases. composed: remove dead code the change touches (skipped for a bug fix), then the integration slice, then the riskiest remaining unknown, then scaffold, then the remaining features. subtraction-first: dead code, scaffold, features. riskiest-first: the step whose failure would invalidate the most downstream work goes first.

scaffold_stubs.description: When true, /planning:design hands off the stub files the change needs with their signatures, and /planning:plan places a stub phase right after phase_order's dead-code removal step (first when there is none). Stub bodies use the language's ordinary not-implemented form. A quoted "true" or "false" is a string, not a boolean, and is invalid.

time_units.description: When true, an estimate or budget of work may be stated in hours, days or weeks; when false, the planning skills use the work_size levels instead. Practice cadence and measurement windows are not estimates and are unaffected. A quoted "true" or "false" is a string, not a boolean, and is invalid.

question_pacing.description: How /planning:interview asks a frontier. round: every ready question in one message. single: the same questions, one per message, largest blast radius first. A request in the session overrides it for that session.

answer_audit_rounds.description: How many rounds /planning:interview counts whose reply accepted every recommendation before it offers /planning:audit-answers, once. 0 never offers.

wayfind_suggest_questions.description: How many questions a /planning:interview ledger's register may hold before the interview suggests /planning:wayfind chart, once, at a round boundary. It suggests when the register holds more than this. 0 never suggests.

pre_confirmed_label.description: A tracker label name. In an unattended run, an item carrying it that states its problem counts as problem-confirmed. Unset: no label pre-confirms; the comment marker in context/problem-framing.md still applies.

wayfind_research_start.description: When /planning:wayfind starts a research item in an interactive session. auto: without asking when the frontier holds no item other than research items, otherwise after the user confirms. confirm: always after the user confirms. An unattended session starts only research items without needs-human, whatever this says.

wayfind_hitl_concurrency.description: The most needs-human items of one /planning:wayfind map that may be claimed at once, across every session. Research items never count against it.

work_size.description: The levels the Brief's Work size uses, per dimension: an ordered map of level name to a one-line quoted description. A dimension set here replaces that dimension's default as a whole. The last level of size is the split trigger, whatever it is named.

appetite.description: How much the human is willing to spend on the work.

default.Small: A contained change the human will spend little on.
default.Medium: A real piece of work the human will fund with some care.
default.Large: A major investment the human accepts.

size.description: How big the work is. The last level means split.

default.Small: One focused change with few moving parts.
default.Medium: Several coordinated changes inside one deliverable.
default.Large: Too big for one deliverable: split it.

uncertainty.description: How much of the work is not yet known.

default.Known: The approach and its unknowns are understood.
default.Knowable: The open points can be settled by looking.
default.Unknown: The open points need experiment or discovery.

interview_surface.description: Settings for the /planning:interview 1:1 page (surface/README.md "Settings layers"). Read from <home>/planning.yaml and <home>/planning.local.yaml; the user file and the data dir's settings.json sit above them, and displayName is not a repository key.

themeTokens.description: CSS token overrides per color mode, each a map of token name to value.

shared_session.description: Starting settings for a /planning:interview shared session. Read once, when a session's state is first created; the owner changes a running session from its Host view.

uploads.description: Whether guests may offer files. The owner still accepts each one.

names.description: What guests see of who answered and voted. full: names. initials: initials and vote counts, never voter ids. someone: guests see "Someone". The owner and leaders always see names.

digest_names.description: Whether the round sent to Claude names who answered, except people a question is aimed at, who are always named.

claude_take.description: When people see Claude's suggestion cards. answer-first: after they answer or vote. always: at once. Each person can switch for themselves.

signoff.description: Whether a leader's lock needs everyone's agreement first. The owner's lock never does.

chat.description: Whether the side chat is on. Chat is never sent to Claude.

follow.description: Whether pages move to a new round when it arrives.

prototype_tiers.description: Which prototype views guests get. screenshot: picture variants. snapshot: self-contained HTML variants. live: a linked prototype server. An empty list shows prototype questions as text. The owner always sees every view.
